body:
Found on getwyrd/wyrd-pdca (template v0.58.0). Related: #473 (recovery adoption of an already-terminal split), #499 (edges that point at the split PARENT — a different case), #589 (the refusal is a traceback).

## What happens

`pdca flow 809 810 776 777`, where:

- `809` is terminal on a split; its children `839`–`843` are PLANNED (the recovery seed case #473 exists for);
- `810` (named) declares `Depends on: 842` — a child of `809`, re-pointed there when `809` was re-planned.

The run is refused before any work:

```
ValueError: issue_810: declared dependency '842' is neither in this batch nor an existing COMPLETE bundle
```

`flow 809` alone works (the children are adopted), and `flow 839 840 841 842 843 810 776 777` works. Only the combination fails: naming the seed AND an id that depends on one of its children.

## Cause

`_drive_and_act` levels the NAMED batch strictly first (`waves.compute_waves(cfg, bundles)` → `check_dep_graph`), and only afterwards splices the seeds' children in at `k=-1`. At the strict check the child `842` is not in the batch and not COMPLETE, so `810`'s edge reads as unresolvable — although the very next statement would have scheduled `842` ahead of it. The comment above the strict call says the check "belongs to the request… and adoption never relaxes it"; here it is not a relaxation, because the prerequisite IS part of the request — the operator named its parent as a recovery seed.

## Fix

Before the strict levelling, collect the names the seeds will offer (their lineage children, transitively through children that are themselves terminal on a split) and let `check_dep_graph` accept a dependency on one of them without adding an edge. The `k=-1` splice already re-levels the whole schedule with the children in it, which is where the edge becomes a real ordering constraint. A dependency that adoption then does NOT take (claimed elsewhere, terminal, refused) is held by the tolerant re-level exactly as a mid-run hold is today — never a mid-run raise.
title: flow: a named id that depends on a split parent's stranded child is refused — the strict dependency check runs before the seed's children are adopted
